title: Adaptive memory profile tuning for long-context Llama/Mistral/Qwen variants
creator: Anya Patel
description: Background: We see recurring OOMs and suboptimal throughput when serving long-context variants (16k+ tokens) of Llama, Mistral and Qwen families. Existing per-model memory profiles are static and tuned for 2k-4k contexts. This ticket scopes an engineering effort to design and implement adaptive memory profiles that change kernel selection, KV cache layout, and quantization choices at runtime based on observed sequence length distributions and batch composition. Goals: reduce peak GPU memory by 20% on long-context workloads, avoid OOMs for grouped client workloads, and keep median latency within 1.2x of baseline for short-context requests.
acceptance_criteria: New adaptive profile API exists and is documented in the runtime config reference.
System demonstrates >=20% reduction in peak GPU memory for synthetic 16k-context workload compared to static profiles.
No increase in 95th percentile latency greater than 25% for mixed short+long workloads in our internal cluster tests.
KV cache correctness validated across rollouts (no cache corruption/regression in unit and integration tests).
Controlled canary rollout plan validated in staging and one dedicated customer with opt-in telemetry.
Benchmarks and cost impact documented in console dashboard for the release.
technical_notes: Design: introduce a 'memory_profile' abstraction with runtime parameters: kv_slot_dtype, kv_blocking_size, kernel_variant_hint, quant_table_id, and max_cached_prefix_tokens.

Runtime heuristics: profile requests per-second by token-length histogram; when 95th percentile token length > threshold, switch to long-context profile that favors bfloat16/4-bit quant path and compact KV layout.
KV cache layout: evaluate two compact layouts (interleaved keys+values vs separate slabs) and prefer slab layout for >8k contexts to reduce pointer overhead.

Batching implications: continuous batching aggregator must respect profile swaps; implement soft boundaries where new batches start with profile selection, but existing in-flight KV caches complete under their original layout to avoid race conditions.

GPU memory accounting: add fine-grained alloc/free markers and a per-model runtime watermark estimator used to decide when to apply proactive micro-quantization (reduce activations precision in late layers for long sequences).
Compatibility: ensure fallbacks to compatible kernel_variant if specialized kernels are unavailable on a node; add telemetry tags to trace fallback events.
Testing: add unit tests for profile selection logic, simulation tests for mixed request streams, and end-to-end stress tests on A100 and 80GB HBM nodes.
Performance: expected trade-offs include slightly increased token compute when using compact KV packing; quantify in benchmark matrix.
Docs: write runtime-1.20 release notes and internal runbook for OOM troubleshooting referencing profile toggles.
Related: ties to ENG-6729 (per-model memory profiles) but shifts to runtime-adaptive mode; coordinate with ENG-7710 (KV cache refactor) and ENG-7601 (batch scheduler changes).
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (dev): implement abstraction and unit tests; run local synthetic benchmarks (internal only).
Phase 2 (staging): enable adaptive profiles on a staging pool; run long-context synthetic workload for 72h and compare watermarks and OOM rates.
Phase 3 (canary): enable for 5% of hosted traffic and 1 dedicated customer with opt-in; monitor latency, memory watermark, fallback telemetry, and KV cache errors for 7 days.
Phase 4 (ramp): increase to 25% then 100% after validation; ship runtime-1.20 with docs and console dashboard indicators for active profile per model.
Rollback: if OOMs or KV cache inconsistencies detected, disable adaptive switching and revert to last stable static profile; follow runbook and open follow-up ENG tickets.
metrics: Peak GPU memory (GB) per model variant (baseline vs adaptive)
Median and 95th percentile latency per token for short (<=2k) and long (>8k) requests
Number of kernel fallback events per node-hour
Cost per 1M tokens for active customers in canary pool
